fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker visible from the road at the driveway entrance to help responders locate the property quickly.
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective posts on both sides to define the access point in low-light or smoky conditions.
• Keep the access drive clear of parked vehicles so emergency apparatus can reach the residence without obstruction.
• Trim trees and shrubs along both sides of the access drive so fire and rescue vehicles can pass without branches blocking mirrors, doors, or ladders.
• Identify and mark a turnaround point on the property so arriving apparatus can reposition without backing long distances down the access drive.
• Keep the open lawn area free of parked vehicles and stored equipment so apparatus can use it as a staging or turnaround area.
• Cut back vegetation on the uphill side of the access drive so slope-related overhang does not obstruct larger vehicles.
• Mark the detached structure with a visible identifier so responders can distinguish it from the main residence during an emergency response.
• Keep a clear walking path between the main residence and the detached structure so responders can move between buildings on foot without obstruction.
• Notify your local fire department of the single-access layout and limited turnaround space so they can note it in pre-incident planning records.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Remove woody debris piles visible near the structures before fire season.
• Thin trees within the cluster closest to the structure to create more open space between them.
• Trim low-hanging branches on scattered trees near the structure to raise the canopy off the ground.
• Cut or mow grass cover close to the structure and any outbuildings.
• Trim shrubs that are growing directly against or touching the structure.
• Keep scattered shrubs separated from nearby tree clusters to avoid connected paths of vegetation toward the structure.
• Clear overhanging branches along the full length of the driveway so emergency vehicles can pass without obstruction.
• Mark the driveway entrance clearly so it is visible to approaching emergency vehicles.
• Keep the driveway surface clear of fallen branches, debris, and encroaching vegetation along its full length.
• Identify and maintain a turnaround area near the structure so emergency vehicles do not have to back out the full length of the driveway.
• Remove dead branches and woody material from beneath tree clusters near the structure.
• Keep grass mowed short in open terrain areas immediately surrounding the structure.
